neighbours.label: noun naming the members of an already-delimited set, at the point where a set-locating phrase is due ('the other booklets', 'every country on the list')
fire: This volume is designed to be read alongside the other volumes.
He has a relative in every town on that route.
The manual should be kept together with the other manuals.
She has tasted a dish from every region on the menu.
This worksheet is intended to be used along with the other worksheets.
We know a family in every village on this map.
This lesson builds on material from the other lessons.
They sent a postcard from every port on the itinerary.
quiet: Several volumes were damaged by the flood last spring.
The town built a new bridge over the river.
Manuals are rarely read by the people who need them.
The region is famous for its smoked cheese.
Worksheets were handed out at the start of class.
A village nearby holds a market every Saturday.
Lessons begin at nine and end at noon.
The port was closed for two days because of fog.

notes: Card: plural nouns after 'the/the other/every' ('the plugins being called', 'the other guides', 'all of the artists listed', 'every country on that list'); output promotes ' in', ' inside', ' within', ' among'. Probes: 'the other booklets/chapters' 0.42-0.60, 'every country on the list' 0.58, 'the tools listed in' 0.25, 'all of the singers featured' 0.18; the same nouns as plain subjects 0.02-0.18; but 'the modules being loaded' 0.005, so the card's top example type did not reproduce.
